executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

c() { echo "$RANDOM" >> a.txt; git add .; git commit -q -m "$1" -m "$2"; }
c "feat: a1" "Closes #1"

Closes #11"

c "feat: a12" "Closes: #14"
c "feat: a13" "BREAKING CHANGE: breaks #15"
c "feat: a14" "BREAKING: #16"
c "feat: a15" "Breaks #17, #18"

EOS
chmod +x /tmp/setup3.sh; /tmp/setup3.sh

echo "=== MD repo ==="; /workspace/executable -r https://github.com/foo/bar 2>&1

import subprocess, pathlib
REF="/workspace/executable"
def run_msg(msg, fmt="markdown"):
    d="/tmp/single2"
    subprocess.run(["bash","-c",f"rm -rf {d} && mkdir -p {d} && cd {d} && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@t.com && git config user.name T && git config commit.gpgsign false && echo hi > a && git add ."],check=True)
    pathlib.Path(d+"/msg.txt").write_text(msg)
    subprocess.run(["bash","-c",f"cd {d} && git commit -q -F msg.txt && rm msg.txt"],check=True)
    pathlib.Path(d+"/.clog.toml").write_text('[clog]\n[sections]\nFeatures=["feat"]\n')
    r=subprocess.run([REF,"-r","https://github.com/foo/bar","-T",fmt],cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)
    return r.stdout.split("changelog written.")[0]
def md_line(msg):
    out=run_msg(msg,"markdown")
    lines=[l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("*")]
    return lines[0] if lines else "(none) "+repr(out)
def json_out(msg):
    return run_msg(msg,"json")
PY

import subprocess,pathlib,os
REF="/workspace/executable"
def run(cfg,args,pre):
    d="/tmp/testrepo"
    for f in os.listdir(d):
        if f.endswith(".md"):
            os.remove(os.path.join(d,f))
    for k,v in (pre or {}).items(): pathlib.Path(d+"/"+k).write_bytes(v if isinstance(v,bytes) else v.encode())
    pathlib.Path(d+"/.clog.toml").write_text(cfg)
    r=subprocess.run([REF]+args,cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    print("args",args,"cfg",repr(cfg),"pre",pre,"rc",r.returncode)
    print(" stdout",r.stdout)
    print(" stderr",r.stderr)
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
        if f.endswith(".md"): print(" ",f,repr(pathlib.Path(d+"/"+f).read_bytes()))

base='[clog]\n[sections]\nFeatures=["feat"]\n'
# same path i/o explicit
run(base,["-i","same.md","-o","same.md"],{"same.md":"OLD-SAME\n"})
# infile exists but unreadable dir etc already
# outfile path same as config file? (overwrite .clog.toml?) risky but in testrepo recreate
# outfile pre-existing but empty
run(base,["-o","out.md"],{"out.md":""})
# outfile pre-existing no trailing newline
run(base,["-o","out.md"],{"out.md":"OLDNO"})
# infile nonexistent, outfile new
run(base,["-i","no.md","-o","out.md"],{})
# infile nonexistent stdout
run(base,["-i","no.md"],{})
# infile specified in cfg pointing nonexistent, outfile cfg preexists: does old outfile content get used or cfg infile (missing) takes precedence resulting no old?
run('[clog]\ninfile="no.md"\noutfile="out.md"\n[sections]\nFeatures=["feat"]\n',[],{"out.md":"OLD-OUT\n"})
# outfile same as infile in cfg separate keys
run('[clog]\ninfile="same.md"\noutfile="same.md"\n[sections]\nFeatures=["feat"]\n',[],{"same.md":"OLD\n"})
# stdout with infile being a directory
run(base,["-i","."],{})
# outfile to /dev/null ?
run(base,["-o","/dev/null"],{})
# outfile to stdout special "-" ?
run(base,["-o","-"],{})
PY
python3 /tmp/file_matrix2.py > /tmp/fm2.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/fm2.txt"}

import subprocess,pathlib

for w in words: candidates.add(w)
for a in words:
 for b in words:
  if a!=b:
   candidates.add(f"{a}-{b}"); candidates.add(f"{a}_{b}"); candidates.add(f"{a}{b}")
# three parts for known
candidates.update(["from-latest-tag","output-format","link-style","git-dir","work-tree"])
found=[]
for k in sorted(candidates):
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/testrepo/.clog.toml").write_text(f'[clog]\n{k} = 12345\n[sections]\nFeatures=["feat"]\n')
    r=subprocess.run([REF],cwd="/tmp/testrepo",capture_output=True,text=True)
    if "Failed to parse" in r.stderr:
        found.append(k)
print("\n".join(found))
PY
python3 /tmp/brute_keys.py

    out.append('"')

def _json_string(s):
